hero.industry: Education / International Student Advisory & Campus Expansion

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Canada: ~70% of revenue; UK and Germany: growing from <10% to significant share; Revenue model: primarily commissions from universities; minimal student fees

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: FY26 flat vs FY25; FY27 target INR80-90cr; Margin: FY27 PAT margin target 20-25%; Order inflow: not specified; Capex/commissioning: Dubai campus to launch Q4FY26, Paris campus Q1FY27, asset-light (rental model)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into Bangladesh (live), Africa, Nepal, Pakistan; Dubai and Paris campuses to enable direct institutional partnerships and third-party agent sourcing; potential to monetize curriculum licensing

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin compression due to fixed cost absorption on lower revenue + aggressive branch expansion (5 new branches) + sponsorship of international education fairs (APAIE, PAL, ICEF); Opex per campus not quantified but asset-light

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing geographic expansion (Dubai, Paris, Africa, Nepal, Pakistan) over buybacks or debt reduction; reinvesting in brand building and campus setup

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautious on current H1FY26 performance but highly confident and excited about near-term campus launches; framing slowdown as temporary, not structural; strong emphasis on brand repositioning from 'immigration' to 'global education'

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Further visa policy tightening in key markets (Canada, UK, Germany); delay in Dubai/Paris licensing; slower-than-expected student conversion post-campuses launch; reliance on university commissions; macroeconomic headwinds affecting education loans

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Dubai campus licensing is imminent (expected within 2 weeks of call date); management has hired a global strategy director with 26+ years’ experience specifically to execute this expansion; campus model allows third-party agent sourcing, reducing dependency on own recruitment

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tighter visa policies and deferred enrollments | Other Indian education consultancies without global campus presence | loser | High | Landmark's campus expansion creates a moat; competitors lack physical presence in key hubs like Dubai/Paris |
